analysis:
The PR is documentation-only: docs/reference/configuration.md adds two rows (head lines 416-417) for DARKBLOOM_TTFT_STREAM_TOOL_CALLS and DARKBLOOM_TTFT_THINK_CONTENT_SEED, both default-on, exact `0` disables, and both forwarded to the LaunchAgent. I examined both supplied base units (lines 1-353 and 354-519 of the base file). The new rows sit in the Engine and scheduler table, after DARKBLOOM_ENGINE_V2_VLM_PARITY_CHECK (base line 415). Only the base text is visible to me, so the head lines are cited from the patch excerpt and I cannot confirm the head numbering.

Security observations. No code or control change is in the diff, so no regression is demonstrated. The rows describe behavior that touches TB-002 and TB-007 and asset A-001 (consumer prompts and completions). (1) Streaming `tool_calls` fragments before each call's closing frame is validated changes the timing of provider output. The text says each call is still validated at frame close, and that required/named calls and other formats are unchanged. Output still passes through the existing encrypted response path. T-008, the fail-closed requirement on encryption failure, is unaffected unless the code path emits plaintext. That code is not in the supplied evidence. (2) Seeding Qwen3-VL content state changes reasoning-parser classification. A wrong split between reasoning and content could leak reasoning text into user-visible content. That is an output-correctness and disclosure concern for the code owner, not provable from docs. The threat model's T-056 notes there is no per-request proof of correct computation, and T-007 already treats provider output as untrusted.

Unverified contracts: whether ToolStreamPreparation.swift and ReasoningPromptProbe.swift exist as described, whether the LaunchAgent passthrough list actually includes both variables, and whether partial tool-call fragments are encrypted per chunk the same way as other SSE chunks. The accompanying source and code changes, if any, should be reviewed against T-008 and T-007. Nothing in this docs diff introduces new attack surface on its own.
